claims.claim: ⚠️ **HAEC is the leading cause of significant morbidity and mortality in Hirschsprung disease (HD).** Mild HAEC can mimic simple gastroenteritis or constipation but needs specialised treatment.
claims.source_text: HAEC (Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis) is the leading cause of significant morbidity and mortality in HD (Hirschsprung Disease) … Mild HAEC can mimic simple gastroenteritis or constipation however requires specialised treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every child with HD is at risk**, before and/or after pull-through surgery.
claims.source_text: All children with HD are at risk of developing HAEC … HAEC may occur before and/or after pull-through surgery for HD
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Higher risk:** under 2 years, undiagnosed HD, trisomy 21, long-segment HD, previous HAEC.
claims.source_text: HAEC is more common in children <2 years of age, those with undiagnosed HD, Trisomy 21, children with long segment HD, and children with previous episodes of HAEC
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** fever, lethargy, anorexia, reduced intake, vomiting, stool pattern (explosive or malodorous diarrhoea, or constipation), rectal bleeding, recent viral illness, previous HAEC. **Most have reduced stool output**, though some have diarrhoea.
claims.source_text: Fever Lethargy Anorexia Reduced oral intake Vomiting Stool (time since last stool, diarrhoea - particularly if explosive in quality, constipation, malodorous) … Most patients with HAEC will have reduced stool output but some may have diarrhoea Rectal bleeding Recent viral infections (respiratory, gastrointestinal) History of recurrent episodes of HAEC
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Establish the HD background:** extent (short segment, long segment, total colonic), current washout regimen, and the definitive procedure (Swenson, Soave or Duhamel).
claims.source_text: Extent of HD Short segment (rectosigmoid) Long segment (proximal colon) Total colonic Current management for HD (rectal bowel washout type and frequency) Type of definitive procedure Swenson - removal of the aganglionated and transition zone bowel … Soave - removal of the aganglionated and transition zone bowel … Duhamel - the ganglionated bowel bought down behind the rectum
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine** for haemodynamic instability, fever, hydration, distension, tenderness and **peritonitis (may be subtle)**. Rectal examination for explosive gas/stool is for a **senior clinician or the surgical team** only.
claims.source_text: Signs of haemodynamic instability Fever Hydration status Abdominal distension Abdominal tenderness Signs of peritonitis (may be subtle) Explosive gas/stool on direct rectal examination (to be performed by senior clinician/surgical team)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal X-ray:** dilated loops, pneumatosis, air-fluid levels, rectosigmoid **cut-off sign** (proximal colonic gas with abrupt absence distally).
claims.source_text: Abdominal x-ray (dilated bowel loops, pneumatosis, air fluid levels, ‘cut off sign’ in rectosigmoid) Cut off sign: gaseous distension of the proximal colon followed by abrupt absence of gas in distal colon
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** gas, FBE (leucocytosis, left shift), UEC, blood culture. **Stool:** MCS, *C. difficile* and rotavirus PCR; consider respiratory PCR.
claims.source_text: Blood gas FBE (leucocytosis, left shift) UEC Blood culture Stool (send for MCS, C. difficile, and rotavirus PCR) Consider respiratory PCR
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Resuscitate shock or hypovolaemia; nil by mouth; IV fluids; surgical review.**
claims.source_text: Resuscitation for signs of shock or hypovolaemia (see Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child) Nil by mouth Intravenous fluids Surgical review
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV antibiotics after discussion with the surgical team:** cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV 8-hourly **plus** metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg (max 500 mg) IV three times daily, **typically for 5 days**.
claims.source_text: IV antibiotics (after discussion with surgical team) Cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV every 8 hours Metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg (max 500 mg) IV 3 times per day Typically 5 days duration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antiemetic:** ondansetron (6 months–18 years) 0.15 mg/kg (max 8 mg) IV 8-hourly.
claims.source_text: Antiemetic Ondansetron (6 months – 18 years) 0.15 mg/kg (max 8 mg) IV every 8 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rectal bowel washout by the surgical team only:** 20 mL/kg warm sodium chloride 0.9%, up to 3 times per day.
claims.source_text: Rectal bowel washout (should only performed by surgical team) 20 mL/kg warm sodium chloride 0.9%, up to 3 times per day
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every child with HD and/or suspected HAEC** with the local paediatric team **and** the paediatric surgical team (local or referral hospital).
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team For all children with HD and/or suspected HAEC All patients should also be discussed with paediatric surgical team (local or referral hospital)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children with HAEC are often transferred to a tertiary centre.**
claims.source_text: Children with HAEC are often transferred to a tertiary centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hirschsprung associated enterocolitis HAEC' (Last updated April 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hirschsprung_associated_enterocolitis_HAEC/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discharge only after discussion with the paediatric surgical team.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge Only after discussion with the paediatric surgical team
